member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronControlSystem.SwitcherInputs
member.summary:
For control systems that have built in switchers (for example, DMPS3), this collection will contain the inputs of the switcher. Since it is a collection of the interface, the programmer will need to read the property to know what the base class of the input is, cast it to that, and then work with it from there. The SwitcherInputs collection will be null for devices that do not have switchers. The index into the SwitcherInputs can also be referenced by the following enums:
for DMPS-200-C
for DMPS-300-C and DMPS-300-C-AEC
for DMPS3-4K-150-C
for DMPS3-4K-100-C
for DMPS3-4K-50
for DMPS3-4K-300-C
for DMPS3-4K-200-C
for DMPS3-4K-350-C
for DMPS3-4K-250-C To make use of a specific input, you will need to check against the type present in the interface and cast/use it from there.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronControlSystem.SwitcherOutputs
member.summary:
For control systems that have built in switchers (for example, DMPS3), this collection will contain the outputs of the switcher. Since it is a collection of the interface, the programmer will need to read the property to know what the base class of the output is, cast it to that, and then work with it from there. The SwitcherOutputs collection will be null for devices that do not have switchers. The index into the SwitcherOutputs can also be referenced by the following enums:
for DMPS-200-C
for DMPS-300-C
for DMPS-300-C-AEC
for DMPS3-4K-150-C
for DMPS3-4K-100-C
for DMPS3-4K-50
for DMPS3-4K-300-C
for DMPS3-4K-200-C
for DMPS3-4K-350-C
for DMPS3-4K-250-C To make use of a specific output, you will need to check against the type present in the interface and cast/use it from there.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronControlSystem.Microphones
member.summary:
For a control system that has microphones, this will be a collection that contains a collection the MicrophoneBase base class. The user can then cast accordingly to a different microphone type using the property. Triggered events for microphones can be monitored by subscribing to the event handler.
See the definition of interface for more information and an example usage.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronControlSystem.Dmps3OutputEqualizer.LimiterSoftKneeOn
member.summary: Enables soft knee limiting. The input only has an effect if LimiterEnable() has been called. When soft knee limiting is enabled, this signifies that limiting will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the limiting less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee limiting is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) limiting. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, it is clipped immediately to the threshold.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronControlSystem.Dmps3OutputEqualizer.LimiterSoftKneeOff
member.summary: Disables soft knee limiting. The input only has an effect if LimiterEnable() has been called. When soft knee limiting is enabled, this signifies that limiting will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the limiting less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee limiting is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) limiting. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, it is clipped immediately to the threshold.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronControlSystem.Dmps3OutputMixer.MixerBypassedFeedback
member.summary: Indicates that the routed audio input is in mixer bypass mode. Mixer bypass mode allows advanced audio to pass through the HDMI switch. The DMPS3 mixers only support stereo PCM. On digital outputs, this means that the audio is routed directly from the audio source without passing through the mixer. The microphone mix and audio controls are not available. On analog outputs the selected source audio will be muted. Mixer bypass mode is only controllable via the DMPS Tool.

member.summary:

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronControlSystem.Dmps3OutputMixer.MinVolume
member.summary: Specifies the minimum volume gain, in tenths of a dB. The MinVolume and MaxVolume properties allow endpoints to be set for volume control. Typically, this property would not be used since the minimum volume can be set through the Front Panel Setup Menus or using the DM Tool in Toolbox. Valid values range from -800 (-80dB) to -400 (-40dB).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronControlSystem.Dmps3OutputMixer.MaxVolume
member.summary: Specifies the maximum volume gain, in tenths of a dB. The MinVolume and MaxVolume properties allow endpoints to be set for volume control. Typically, this property would not be used since the minimum volume can be set through the Front Panel Setup Menus or using the DM Tool in Toolbox. Valid values range from -300 (-30dB) to 100 (10dB).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronControlSystem.Dmps3OutputMixer.StartupVolume
member.summary: Specifies the startup volume in tenths of a dB. The startup volume is the volume level that will be set when the system is turned on. Valid values range from -800 (-80dB) to 100 (10dB).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronControlSystem.Dmps3AttachableOutputMixer.MixerBypassedFeedback
member.summary: Indicates that the routed audio input is in mixer bypass mode. Mixer bypass mode allows advanced audio to pass through the HDMI switch. The DMPS3 mixers only support stereo PCM. On digital outputs, this means that the audio is routed directly from the audio source without passing through the mixer. The microphone mix and audio controls are not available. On analog outputs the selected source audio will be muted. Mixer bypass mode is only controllable via the DMPS Tool.

member.name: T:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.eDeviceCapabilities
member.summary: This enum can be used in some device constructors to allow expanded capabilities. For example, some panels were upgraded to allow them to receive ramps instead of discrete analog packets which allows for less network traffic and smoother ramping. Since newer versions may support a capability that older versions do not, we allow the programmer to force using the new capability, since the device model is set to use the older capabilities for compatibility.
member.remarks: Not all devices support all capability flags. Also, these flags often rely on the device having specific versions of firmware or later, and device release notes should be consulted.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.eDeviceCapabilities.None
member.summary: No extra capabilities specified.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.eDeviceCapabilities.SendRampsInsteadOfDiscreteAnalogs
member.summary: This capability allows SIMPL# Pro to send ramps to a device. If the programmer uses the CreateRamp call on a device, a ramping packet will be sent to the device rather than a series of discrete values. Care must be taken to know if the actual device supports ramping (see the specific device class for any version requirements.)

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.BlackNovaKeypadButton.EnableBuzzer
member.summary: Property to activate/deactivate the buzzer beep sound on the button press event. true = Buzzer Enabled; false = Buzzer Disabled. The default value (on device power-up) is false.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.BlackNovaKeypadButton.IndicatorSmoothing
member.summary: Property to activate/deactivate the indicator smoothing on the button press event. true = Indicator smoothing enabled; false = Indicator smoothing disabled. The default value (on device power-up) is false.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.BlackNovaKeypadButton.InactiveIndicatorColor
member.summary: Property to set the inactive indicator color. The color in RGB HEX string format (RRGGBB) that is applied to button feedback LED indicator when it is ON (Active/Pressed). For example: F70099. The values with the wrong format are ignored.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.BlackNovaKeypadButton.ActiveIndicatorColor
member.summary: Property to set the active indicator color. The color in RGB HEX string format (RRGGBB) that is applied to button feedback LED indicator when it is OFF (Inactive/Released). For example: A70B16. The values with the wrong format are ignored.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3AecOutputEqualizer.LimiterSoftKneeOn
member.summary: Enables soft knee limiting. The input only has an effect if LimiterEnable() has been called. When soft knee limiting is enabled, this signifies that limiting will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the limiting less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee limiting is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) limiting. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, it is clipped immediately to the threshold.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3AecOutputEqualizer.LimiterSoftKneeOff
member.summary: Disables soft knee limiting. The input only has an effect if LimiterEnable() has been called. When soft knee limiting is enabled, this signifies that limiting will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the limiting less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee limiting is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) limiting. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, it is clipped immediately to the threshold.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3AudioOutputMixer.MixerBypassedFeedback
member.summary:
Indicates that the routed audio input is in mixer bypass mode. Mixer bypass mode allows advanced audio to pass through the HDMI switch. The DMPS3 mixers only support stereo PCM. On digital outputs, this means that the audio is routed directly from the audio source without passing through the mixer. The microphone mix and audio controls are not available. On analog outputs the selected source audio will be muted. Mixer bypass mode is only controllable via the DMPS Tool.
The event will trigger with .

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3AudioOutputEqualizer.LimiterSoftKneeOn
member.summary: Enables soft knee limiting. The input only has an effect if LimiterEnable() has been called. When soft knee limiting is enabled, this signifies that limiting will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the limiting less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee limiting is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) limiting. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, it is clipped immediately to the threshold.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3AudioOutputEqualizer.LimiterSoftKneeOff
member.summary: Disables soft knee limiting. The input only has an effect if LimiterEnable() has been called. The slower onset can make the limiting less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee limiting is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) limiting. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, it is clipped immediately to the threshold.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3AudioOutputEqualizer.LimiterThreshold
member.summary: Sets the limiting threshold. Valid values range from -800 (-80dB) to 0 (0dB) Once the signal exceeds the threshold, the limiter will clip the level to the threshold value. In this way, the output signal level will never exceed the threshold.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3AudioOutputEqualizer.LimiterAttack
member.summary: Sets the attack time, which is the time in milliseconds that it takes the limiter to start clipping the signal level after the threshold has been exceeded. Valid values range from 1 (0.1ms) to 3000 (300ms).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3AudioOutputEqualizer.LimiterRelease
member.summary: Sets the release time, which is the time over which the limiter will stop clipping after the signal crosses under the threshold. Valid values range from 1 (1ms) to 1000 (1000ms)

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3AudioOutputEqualizer.LimiterRatio
member.summary: Sets the limiter ratio, which controls the amount of gain reduction to apply when the mic signal level exceeds the threshold. Valid values range from 1 (1:1) to 10 (10:1).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3DmHdmiOutputMixer.MixerBypassedFeedback
member.summary: Indicates that the routed audio input is in mixer bypass mode. Mixer bypass mode allows advanced audio to pass through the HDMI switch. The DMPS3 mixers only support stereo PCM. On digital outputs, this means that the audio is routed directly from the audio source without passing through the mixer. The microphone mix and audio controls are not available. On analog outputs the selected source audio will be muted. Mixer bypass mode is only controllable via the DMPS Tool.

member.summary: Reports the VU meter feedback value, when VU feedback is enabled. Reported values will range from 0 to 8.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Dmps3SipDialer.Init
member.summary: Set SIP configuration parameters.
member.remarks: Each field must be separated by the & symbol, with no spaces between fields. FIELDS: USER = The local dialing extension of the touch screen. AUTH = The server login username. PW = The server login password. SIPSRV = The server IP address (xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx). SIPPORT = The server port number in decimal. DOMAIN = The server domain. REALM = The server realm. MODE = The panel mode, i.e., SERVER or PEER AUTO = The panel auto function mode, i.e., NONE or DS. RCONFIG = The path of the configuration file to download, for use with the AUTO mode setting. DNAME = The display name of the touch screen. PORT = The port number that the local SIP client will use. SRVNAME = The display name of the SIP server (for information only). PAGE = The paging group the touch screen belongs to. Multiple group names must be separated by commas with no spaces: Example: OUTSIDE,PATIO. PROXYIP = IP address of a proxy server, or NONE to clear. NAMESRV = IP address of an SIP name server, or NONE to clear. STUNDOM = IP address of a STUN Domain server, or NONE to clear. STUNIP = IP address of a STUN server, or NONE to clear. SPSTR =The extra string to include in the SIP INVITE. DND = The Do not Disturb feature preset, i.e. On or Off

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.Usbc.DisabledByHdcpFeedback
member.summary:
Indicates that the corresponding output has been disabled as the result of a failure during HDCP authentication. This occurs when HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) is detected at the input, but the display or other loopback device is not HDCP compliant. This also occurs when the maximum number of display devices that can be used with the video source (based on the application of keys and KSVs) has been exceeded.For more information about keys and KSVs, see HDCP. This is supported for some of the devices only. 'true' = Output disabled by HDCP; 'false' = Output not disabled by HDCP
The event will trigger with .

This occurs when HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) is detected at the input, but the display or other loopback device is not HDCP compliant. member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DeviceSupport.HdmiOutWithColorSpaceMode.VideoWallMode
member.summary:
Property to specify which portion of the wall image to display in wall mode, where each display in a wall of displays shows a portion of the image. Displays can be laid out in configurations up to 8x8. Each display requires connection to a separate scaler. The wall mode can be specified using the following method: The video portion can be defined using the 4 digit decimal value WHXY where:
W is the width of the wall (number of columns that make up the wall) H is the height of the wall (number of rows) X is the horizontal position of that display on the wall Y is the vertical position of that display on the wall For example, for a 2x2 video wall the upper left would be 2211, the upper right 2221, the lower left 2212 and the lower right 2222. 0 disables the wall mode. This property is supported only by "Dm100xStrBase". This method is not supported for the "HdmiOut" on the "DmNvxE30","DmNvxE30C","DmNvxE31" and "DmNvxE31C" devices.

member.summary:

Displays can be laid out in configurations up to 8x8. Each display requires connection to a separate scaler. The wall mode can be specified using the following method: The video portion can be defined using the 4 digit decimal value WHXY where:
W is the width of the wall (number of columns that make up the wall) H is the height of the wall (number of rows) X is the horizontal position of that display on the wall Y is the vertical position of that display on the wall For example, for a 2x2 video wall the upper left would be 2211, the upper right 2221, the lower left 2212 and the lower right 2222. 0 disables the wall mode. This property is supported only by "Dm100xStrBase". This method is not supported for the "HdmiOut" on the "DmNvxE30","DmNvxE30C","DmNvxE31" and "DmNvxE31C" devices.

member.name: T:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eHdcpTransmitterMode
member.summary: Enum to define HDCP Mode set for output.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eHdcpTransmitterMode.Auto
member.summary:
Auto Mode.
Scaler outputs:
When non-HDCP content is routed, the content will pass through and not be authenticated until HDCP content is routed.
When HDCP content is routed the scaler should latch onto the highest HDCP level supported by the downstream device.
The device should not attempt to re-authenticate unless hot-plugged or downstream device HDCP support level changes.
This is the default mode for Scaler outputs.
Eg. 4K-HDO connected to DMC-4K-HD (Support Level 2.x)
Input (Non-HDCP) | Sink (Non-HDCP)
Input HDCP | Sink (HDCP 2.2)
Input HDCP 2.2 | Sink (HDCP 2.2)
Input Non-HDCP | Sink (HDCP 2.2)
Input HDCP | Sink (HDCP 2.2)
Output Hot-plugged or downstream HDCP support level change:
Input non-HDCP | Sink (Non-HDCP)
For Non-Scaler outputs this mode is invalid.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eHdcpTransmitterMode.FollowInput
member.summary:
Follow Input Mode.
Authenticate each time the input sync changes it state. The output should authenticate to the level reported at the Input.
This is the default mode for Non-Scaler outputs.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eHdcpTransmitterMode.ForceHighest
member.summary:
Force to authenticate to the highest level HDCP.
For Scaler outputs in this mode, authenticate each time the input sync changes it state.
The output should authenticate to the level reported at the Input.
For Non-Scaler outputs in this mode, authenticate to the highest level HDCP supported by the downstream device.
This should be done regardless of the input side.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eHdcpTransmitterMode.NeverAuthenticate
member.summary: Never Authenticate (Blank if the Input is HDCP encrypted).

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eHdcpTransmitterMode.NotSupported
member.summary: HDCP Mode is not supported.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.Card.DmHdmiOutput.DisabledByHdcpFeedback
member.summary: Indicates that the corresponding output has been disabled as the result of a failure during HDCP authentication. This occurs when HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) is detected at the input, but the display or other loopback device is not HDCP compliant. This also occurs when the maximum number of display devices that can be used with the video source (based on the application of keys and KSVs) has been exceeded.For more information about keys and KSVs, see HDCP. 'true' = Output disabled by HDCP; 'false' = Output not disabled by HDCP

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.Card.Dmps3DmOutputBackend.USBRoutedTo
member.summary:
Specifies the USB route of the DM Outputs or the DM Inputs.
For a DMPS3-4K-200-C, USB can be routed to SwitcherInputs[7] (eDmps34K200CInputs.Dm1).
For a DMPS3-4K-250-C, USB can be routed to SwitcherInputs[7] (eDmps34K250CInputs.Dm1).
For a DMPS3-4K-300-C, USB can be routed to SwitcherInputs[7] (eDmps34K300CInputs.Dm1)and SwitcherInputs[8] (eDmps34K300CInputs.Dm2).
For a DMPS3-4K-350-C, USB can be routed to SwitcherInputs[7] (eDmps34K350CInputs.Dm1)and SwitcherInputs[8] (eDmps34K350CInputs.Dm2).

remarks.para: Assigning null will disconnect the route.

member.exception: If the specified input or output is is illegal for a USB route.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.Card.Dmps3DmOutput.USBRoutedTo
member.summary:
Specifies the USB route of the DM Outputs.
For a DMPS-200-C, USB can be routed to SwitcherOutputs[2].
For a DMPS-300-C, USB can be routed to SwitcherOutputs[3] and SwitcherOutputs[4].

remarks.para: Assigning null will disconnect the route.
Assigning SwitcherInputs[6] will connect to DM Input 6.
Assigning SwitcherInputs[7] will connect to DM Input 7.
Assigning SwitcherOutputs[2] will connect to DM Output 2 (DMPS-200-C only).
Assigning SwitcherOutputs[3] will connect to DM Output 3 (DMPS-300-C only).
Assigning SwitcherOutputs[4] will connect to DM Output 4 (DMPS-300-C only).

member.exception: If the specified input or output is is illegal for a USB route.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.eDmSwitcherCards.DmcS
member.summary: The DMC-S(DSP) is a DigitalMedia 8G™ multimode fiber video card compatible with the input card slots of a DigitalMedia switcher. The video card provides (1) DigitalMedia SC input connector labeled DM IN that receives video, audio, HDCP, EDID and USB data from a DM transmitter or output card, with a maximum length of 1000 feet.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.eDmSwitcherCards.DmcSDsp
member.summary: The DMC-S(DSP) is a DigitalMedia 8G™ multimode fiber video card compatible with the input card slots of a DigitalMedia switcher. The video card provides (1) DigitalMedia SC input connector labeled DM IN that receives video, audio, HDCP, EDID and USB data from a DM transmitter or output card, with a maximum length of 1000 feet.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.eDmSwitcherCards.DmcS2
member.summary: The DMC-S2 is a DigitalMedia 8G™ single mode fiber video card compatible with the input card slots of a DigitalMedia switcher. The video card provides (1) DigitalMedia LC input connector labeled DM IN that receives video, audio, HDCP, EDID and USB data from a DM transmitter or output card, with a maximum length over 10 miles. The RCA audio output (labeled AUDIO OUT L/R) breaks out the stereo audio signal from the DM input and passes it through to feed a CNX-PAD8A, AAE, or other multi-room audio distribution system. The card also provides one HDMI output port labeled HDMI OUT for feedthrough to a local display device.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.eDmSwitcherCards.DmcS2Dsp
member.summary: The DMC-S2-DSP is a DigitalMedia 8G™ single mode fiber video card compatible with the input card slots of a DigitalMedia switcher. The video card provides (1) DigitalMedia LC input connector labeled DM IN that receives video, audio, HDCP, EDID and USB data from a DM transmitter or output card, with a maximum length over 10 miles. The RCA audio output (labeled AUDIO OUT L/R) breaks out the stereo audio signal from the DM input and passes it through to feed a CNX-PAD8A, AAE, or other multi-room audio distribution system. The card also provides one HDMI output port labeled HDMI OUT for feedthrough to a local display device. The DSP model includes an internal DSP to enable the simultaneous distribution of uncompressed 7.1 channel HD surround sound and 2-channel audio.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.eDmSwitcherCards.DmcF
member.summary: The DMC-F is a video card compatible with the input card slots of a DigitalMedia switcher. The DMC-F provides one DigitalMedia fiber input labeled FIBER IN. The "D" input receives video and audio from the "D" output of a DM fiber transmitter or output card. The "M" input receives HDCP, EDID, and USB data from the "M" input of the DM fiber transmitter or output card. The RCA audio output (labeled AUDIO OUT L/R) breaks out the stereo audio signal from the DM input and passes it through to feed a CNX-PAD8A, AAE, or other multi-room audio distribution system.The DMC-F also provides one HDMI local output port labeled HDMI OUT for feedthrough to a local device.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.eDmSwitcherCards.DmcFDsp

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.eDmSwitcherCards.DmcHd
member.summary: The DMC-HD is an HDMI video card compatible with the input card slots of the DigitalMedia switcher. The DMC-HD provides 1 HDMI input labeled HDMI IN. The USB HID port is a Type B port for connection to a USB host. The DMC-HD also provides one HDMI local output port labeled HDMI OUT for feedthrough to a local device.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.eDmSwitcherCards.DmcSdi

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.eDmSwitcherCards.DmcStroAV
member.summary: The DMC-STRO is a streaming output card with video and audio mixing capabilities which can generate streams of up to 25 megabits. To be matched precisely to your environment the card has been designed to allow flexibility in network design; the stream can either be routed out via the Content LAN port, or the DM's internal Ethernet. In automatic mode (default), the DMC-STRO will stream out via the Content LAN port if link is detected, otherwise it will use the internal DM Ethernet. This card also provides a number of streaming methods. Please review all available Session Initiation options to select the proper stream type that best suits your environment.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.DmcStrControl.eSessionInitiation.ByReceiver
member.summary: The card waits for a connection from a receiving device. The client connects to the URL specified in and the server connects to the URL specified in the . This is a unicast stream. If multiple clients connect, the packets are duplicated for each client. For example, if the DMC-STRO is configured to provide a 5000kbps stream and one client connects, 5000kbps is generated. However, if a second client connects, the stream is duplicated consuming 10kbps total. The DMC-STRO can support up to 25000kbps after which point, degradation in the video quality may be observed. There is no limit imposed to the number of connections allowed.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.DmcStrControl.eSessionInitiation.MulticastViaRTSP
member.summary: Multicast via RTSP. The device still accepts RTSP requests, but sends back a multicast address instead of unicasting. This is useful when you need to setup one stream and then have all touch panels connect to it. The multicast address is specified in . The client connects to the address specified in and the server connects to the URL specified in the .

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Cards.DmcStrControl.eSessionInitiation.MulticastViaUDP
member.summary: The device streams raw UPD to a multicast address and does not have RTSP. The stream is always on and clients can connect to it (this also has the advantage of not needing to restart the stream if something goes wrong).

member.summary:
Indicates that the audio source is not compliant with SMPTE SDI specifications. The output remains 'true' for as long as noncompliant audio is detected. Noncompliant audio is corrected by default. 'true' = Audio noncompliant; 'false' = Audio OK
The event will trigger with when a part of a switcher.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.SdiPort.CorrectNoncompliantAudio
member.summary: Applies audio correction when noncompliant audio is detected (Noncompliant_Audio_DetectedFeedback is 'true'). Noncompliant audio is corrected by default. In some cases, correction can affect the M value of the analog/SDI signal, which in turn leads to unstable video. If this occurs, the M value can be adjusted manually (via the "force M value" ). Alternatively, audio correction can be turned off (via the "Prevent_Noncompliant_Audio_Correction").

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.SdiPort.CorrectNoncompliantAudioFeedback
member.summary:
Indicates that audio correction is being applied. The output remains high for as long as audio correction is on. 'true' = Audio correction is on; 'false' = No audio correction.
The event will trigger with when a part of a switcher.
The event will trigger with when a part of a DMCI.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.SdiPort.PreventNoncompliantAudioCorrection
member.summary: Stops audio correction of the input. This can be used when audio correction results in video problems. When correction is prevented, audio may or may not be heard. Alternatively, audio correction can be left on and the M value of the video signal adjusted manually (via the "force M value" ).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.SdiPort.PreventNoncompliantAudioCorrectionFeedback
member.summary:
Indicates that audio correction is being prevented. The output remains 'true for as long as audio correction is off. 'true' = Audio correction is off; 'false' = Audio correction is on.
The event will trigger with when a part of a switcher.
The event will trigger with when a part of a DMCI.

member.summary:

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Streaming.DmNvxControl.StillImageDetectionFeedback
member.summary:
Property to report still image detection. (TX Mode) There is a sync at the selected input, and there is no motion within the image for more than 5 seconds (RX Mode) There is a sync at the selected input or stream, that is feeding the output, and there is no motion within the image for more than 5 seconds 0 = No Sync (No source) 1 = Motion is detected, and Sync is present for currently selected input and stream 2 = Still image detected for Currently selected input or stream
The event will trigger with .

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.H264StreamingMethods.Automatic
member.summary: Automatic (default): Starts the H.264 stream as a multicast RTSP stream. Automatic will add +8 to the outgoing NVX video stream multicast address. For example, if the NVX video multicast address is 239.8.0.0, the H.264 multicast address will be 239.8.0.8.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.H264StreamingMethods.Multicast
member.summary: Multicast via RTSP H.264: Specifies a custom multicast RTSP stream. Wait for an incoming connection from a client. The stream is sent to the multicast IP address specified in the RTSP Multicast Address text box.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.H264StreamingMethods.Unicast
member.summary: Unicast via RTSP H.264: Specifies a unicast RTSP H.264 stream. Wait for an incoming connection from a client. When the client connects, the initiation session parameters are exchanged and the stream begins.

member.name: T:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.H264StreamTypes
member.summary: Enum to specify the H264 stream type.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.H264StreamTypes.MPEG2TSRTP
member.summary: MPEG2TSRTP (default): Allows to transmit MPEG-2 TS streams with RTP encapsulation. Only one port number is consumed by the encapsulation. The default port number is 4570. NOTE: MPEG2TSRTP supports the streaming of HDCP content to a Crestron HDCP streaming receiver. Refer to the documentation of the receiving or transmitting device to verify that the device can encapsulate the stream in MPEG-2 TS.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.H264StreamTypes.MPEG2TSUDP
member.summary: MPEG2TSUDP: Allows to transmit MPEG-2 TS UDP streams. Only one port number is consumed by the encapsulation. The default port number is 4570. NOTE: MPEG2TSUDP is recommended for multicast UDP streams. MPEG2TSUDP supports the streaming of HDCP content to a Crestron HDCP streaming receiver. Refer to the documentation of the receiving or transmitting device to verify that the device can encapsulate the stream in MPEG-2 TS.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.H264StreamTypes.RTP
member.summary: RTP: Allows to stream the audio and video as separate RTP streams. Each RTP stream uses a different port. Refer to the documentation of the receiving or transmitting device to verify that this setting should be used.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.PhantomPowerOn
member.summary: Enables the 48V phantom power supply. (Phantom power is required by condenser microphones, but should be disengaged for dynamic microphones.)

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.PhantomPowerOff
member.summary: Disables the 48V phantom power supply. (Phantom power is required by condenser microphones, but should be disengaged for dynamic microphones.)

member.summary: Enables the noise gate.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.GateDisable
member.summary: Disables the noise gate.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.CompressorEnable
member.summary: Enables compression (gain reduction)

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.CompressorDisable
member.summary: Disables compression (gain reduction)

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.CompressorSoftKneeOn
member.summary: Enables the soft knee compression. The input only has an effect if compression is enabled. When soft knee compression is enabled, this signifies that compression will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the compression less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee compression is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) compression. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, compression is immediately applied at the specified ratio.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.CompressorSoftKneeOff
member.summary: Enables the soft knee compression. The input only has an effect if compression is enabled. When soft knee compression is enabled, this signifies that compression will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the compression less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee compression is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) compression. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, compression is immediately applied at the specified ratio.

member.summary: Indicates that the mic signal level has exceeded 50% of the maximum level supported by the hardware, or 2dB below the input clip level. This signifies a mic level that is too hot.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.GateLevel
member.summary: Sets the threshold for gating. The noise gate is enabled for as long as the gate is enabled. Valid values range from -800 (-80dB, full mute) to 0 (0dB). Once the microphone audio rises above the set GateLevel the gate opens, allowing the signal to pass through.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.GateThreshold
member.summary: Sets the threshold for gating. The noise gate is enabled for as long as the gate is enabled. Valid values range from -800 (-80dB, full mute) to 0 (0dB). Once the microphone audio rises above the set GateLevel the gate opens, allowing the signal to pass through.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.GateDepth
member.summary: Sets the decibel level to go to when the gate is closed (1 = 0.1dB). Valid values range from -800 (-80dB, full mute) to 0 (0dB, minimum noise attenuation). Setting the depth above a full mute can help eliminate a swooping sound that can occur when the gate closes and opens.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.GateAttack
member.summary: Sets the time, in milliseconds, that it takes for the noise gate to fully open after the signal exceeds the GatingThreshold. This prevents short spikes in the input signal level, such as coughing, from opening the gate. Valid values range from 1 (1ms) to 250 (250ms).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.GateRelease
member.summary: Sets the time, in milliseconds, over which the noise gate will close. This prevents the sound from stopping too abruptly—for example, during brief pauses in speech. Valid values range from 0 (0ms) to 5000 (5000ms, or 5s), with 1000 to 3000 (1s to 3s) being the most usable range.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.GateDecay
member.summary: Sets the time, in milliseconds, over which the noise gate will close. This prevents the sound from stopping too abruptly—for example, during brief pauses in speech. Valid values range from 0 (0ms) to 5000 (5000ms, or 5s), with 1000 to 3000 (1s to 3s) being the most usable range.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.GateHold
member.summary: Sets the gate hold time in milliseconds. The gate hold time over which the gate will close. Valid analog values range from 1 (1 ms) to 200 (200 ms).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.CompressorThreshold
member.summary: Sets the threshold for compression (gain reduction). Valid values range from -800 (-80dB) to 0 (0dB), where 1 = 0.1dB. Once the microphone signal exceeds the threshold, its gain is reduced by the specified compression ratio.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.CompressorAttack
member.summary: Sets the attack time, which is the time in milliseconds that it takes the compressor to start compressing after the threshold has been reached. Valid values range from 1 (0.1ms) to 250 (25ms), where 1 = 0.1ms.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.CompressorRelease
member.summary: Sets the release time, which is the time over which the compressor will stop compressing after the signal crosses under the threshold, where 1 = 1ms. Valid values range from 1 (1ms) to 1000 (1000ms).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.CompressorRatio
member.summary: Sets the compression ratio, which controls the amount of gain reduction to apply when the mic signal level exceeds the threshold. For example, with a 2:1 ratio, for every 2 decibels the input signal increases, the output is allowed to increase only by 1 decibel. Valid values range from 1 (1:1) to 10 (10:1).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.CompressorHold
member.summary: Sets the compression hold, the time (in milliseconds), over which the compression will start after the signal crosses under the threshold. Valid values range from 1 to 200, where 1 = 1 ms.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.EqHighBandFrequency
member.summary: Specifies the frequency for the corresponding High Band. Valid frequency ranges are as follows: 3200 (3.2kHz) to 12800 (12.8kHz)

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.EqHighBandGain

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.EqHighMidBandGain

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.EqLowMidBandFrequency

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DmMdMicrophone.EqLowMidBandGain

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.IOutputEqualizerLimiter.LimiterReleaseFeedback
member.summary: Retrieves the release time, which is the time over which the limiter will stop clipping after the signal crosses under the threshold.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.IOutputEqualizerLimiter.LimiterSoftKneeOff
member.summary: Disables soft knee limiting. The input only has an effect if LimiterEnable() has been called. When soft knee limiting is enabled, this signifies that limiting will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the limiting less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee limiting is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) limiting. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, it is clipped immediately to the threshold.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.IOutputEqualizerLimiter.LimiterSoftKneeOffFeedback
member.summary: Indicates that soft knee limiting is disabled. When soft knee limiting is enabled, this signifies that limiting will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the limiting less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee limiting is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) limiting. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, it is clipped immediately to the threshold.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.IOutputEqualizerLimiter.LimiterSoftKneeOn
member.summary: Enables soft knee limiting. The input only has an effect if LimiterEnable() has been called. When soft knee limiting is enabled, this signifies that limiting will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the limiting less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee limiting is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) limiting. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, it is clipped immediately to the threshold.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.IOutputEqualizerLimiter.LimiterSoftKneeOnFeedback
member.summary: Indicates that soft knee limiting is enabled. When soft knee limiting is enabled, this signifies that limiting will be applied gradually, depending on how far the signal is from the threshold. The slower onset can make the limiting less noticeable, especially when using high compression ratios. When soft knee limiting is disabled, this will apply normal (hard knee) limiting. This signifies that as soon as the signal exceeds the threshold, it is clipped immediately to the threshold.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.IOutputEqualizerLimiter.LimiterThreshold
member.summary: Sets the limiting threshold. Once the signal exceeds the threshold, the limiter will clip the level to the threshold value. In this way, the output signal level will never exceed the threshold.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.IOutputEqualizerLimiter.LimiterThresholdFeedback
member.summary: Retrieves the limiting threshold. Once the signal exceeds the threshold, the limiter will clip the level to the threshold value. In this way, the output signal level will never exceed the threshold.

member.summary: Indicates that the routed audio input is in mixer bypass mode. Mixer bypass mode allows advanced audio to pass through the HDMI switch. The DMPS3 mixers only support stereo PCM. On digital outputs, this means that the audio is routed directly from the audio source without passing through the mixer. The microphone mix and audio controls are not available. On analog outputs the selected source audio will be muted. Mixer bypass mode is only controllable via the DMPS Tool.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.IBasicHdmiOutput.DisabledByHdcpFeedback
member.summary: Indicates that the stream has been disabled as the result of a failure during HDCP authentication. This occurs when HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) is detected at the input, but the display or other loopback device is not HDCP compliant. This also occurs when the maximum number of display devices that can be used with the video source (based on the application of keys and KSVs) has been exceeded.
member.returns: 'true' = Output disabled by HDCP; 'false = Output not disabled by HDCP

member.summary:
Pause the streaming.
Note: although the incoming video to the encoder is paused (frozen),the stream will continue playing and the elapsed time counter will continue in the paused state.This allows a freeze frame to be displayed if the user does not want live video to be transmitted.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Dmps3SystemControlWithStreaming.StreamingDeviceReadyFeedback
member.summary:
Indicates that the device is ready to start streaming or preview video.
The device may not be ready if the IP address has changed or another system event has caused a re-configuration.
The appropriate feedback for those parameters should be checked to ensure that the stream starts correctly.
Start signals will be ignored until the device is ready to start streaming.
'true' = Device is ready; 'false' = Device is not ready.
The event will trigger with .

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Dmps3SystemControlWithStreaming.StreamingDeviceProcessingBusy
member.summary:
Indicates that the streaming device is changing state (starting the stream, stopping the stream, etc) and is busy.
Please wait until the signal is 'false' before sending commands to the device.
'true' = busy; 'false' = not busy
The event will trigger with .

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Dmps3SystemControlWithStreaming.StreamingAudioMuteFeedback
member.summary:
Indicates that streaming output audio is muted.
The event will trigger with .

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Dmps3SystemControlWithStreaming.StreamingAudioUnmuteFeedback
member.summary:
Indicates that the output audio is not muted.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Dmps3SystemControlWithStreaming.StreamPasswordProtectionEnableFeedback

member.name: T:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eDmSessionInitiation
member.summary: Streaming session initiation status enum definition for .

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eDmSessionInitiation.ByReceiver
member.summary: Unicast session initiated by receiver via RSTP. For example, the DMCI-DMC-STR card creates a connection to a server(transmitting device). Specify the server to which the DMC-STR should connect in .

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eDmSessionInitiation.ByTransmitter
member.summary:
Unicast session initiated by transmitter.
For example, the DMCI-DMC-STR waits for a transmitter to connect and then starts the stream. The connection source address is reported on . In this case, there is no RSTP exchange, so the decoder must be prepared to receive the stream.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eDmSessionInitiation.MulticastViaRTSP
member.summary:
Multicast session initiated by receiver(s) via RSTP.
This is similar to Mode 0 (ByReceiver).
Specify the server to which the DMC-STR should connect in . In this mode DMCI-DMC-STR should NOT be configured to connect directly to the multicast address.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eDmSessionInitiation.MulticastViaUDP
member.summary:
Multicast raw UDP session initiated by transmitter.
In this case, the DMCI-DMC-STR connects to an active multicast stream. Specify the multicast address to which the DMCI-DMC-STR should connect using .

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.AdvancedHdmi.HDMIAudioChannelsFeedback
member.summary: Reports the number of audio channels detected. Values will range from 0d to 8d. A value of 0d signifies that no audio is present or that the channel count could not be determined because the audio format is compressed ("HDMI_Audio_Format_fb" = 16d).

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.AdvancedHdmi.HDMIAudioCompFeedback
member.summary: Reports the source gain compensation being applied at the HDMI IN 3 input.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.AdvancedHdmi.HDMIAudioComp
member.summary: Adjusts the source gain compensation at the HDMI 3 input. Valid values range from -100d (-10dB) to +100d (+10dB). The source gain compensation only has an effect on the analog audio output (AUDIO OUT), and has no effect on the DM or HDMI outputs.The total gain at the output will never exceed 0dB, as the output range is -80dB to 0dB. If the input compensation plus the output volume exceeds 0dB, the output will be limited to 0dB. Changes that exceed 0dB will have no effect.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.HdmiInputWithCEC.Priority
member.summary:
For HD-RX-4K-210 switches: Gets/Sets the input priority. The range is 1 to 4 based on the number of local inputs on the device. Transmitters connected to DM Lite inputs will each have a separate Priority setting with a maximum value equal to the total number of transmitter inputs. The valid values for CCE-4100 and CCE-4200 are 1 to 255. This property only works if Auto Route is enabled. For HD-MD switches: Get/Set the Input Priority. Priority routing will give the dealer the ability to select which inputs they feel are most important to the end user when auto routing.
The event will trigger with . This property is supported by HD-RX-4K-210, HD-MD-4x1-4KZ-E, HD-MD4x2-4KZ-E and not supportedby HD-MD-4x4-4KZ-E, HD-MD-8x4-4KZ-E and HD-MD-8x8-4KZ-E switches.

member.summary:
Indicates that the HDMI output has been disabled as the result of a failure during HDCP authentication. This occurs when HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) is detected at the input, but the display or other loopback device is not HDCP compliant. This also occurs when the maximum number of display devices that can be used with the video source (based on the application of keys and KSVs) has been exceeded. For more information about keys and KSVs, see HDCP. 'true' = Output disabled by HDCP; 'false' = Output not disabled by HDCP
The event will trigger with when a part of a switcher.
The event will trigger with when a part of a DMCI.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.InputCardHdmiOutPort.BlankedByHdcp2xFeedback
member.summary:
Indicates that the HDMI output (HDMI OUT) has been blanked as the result of a failure during HDCP 2.2 authentication. This occurs when HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) is detected at the HDMI input, but the display or other loopback device is not HDCP 2.2 compliant--and is therefore blanked. This property may not be supported for the specified device. 'true' = HDMI OUT blanked by HDCP 2.2; 'false' = HDMI OUT not blanked disabled by HCDP 2.2
The event will trigger with when a part of a switcher.
The event will trigger with when a part of a DMCI.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.DmNvxUsbInput.HostSelection
member.summary:
Property to select which USB-C port is the Host. Remote devices enumerate to the PC connected to the Host port. shall have the following behavior: USB Host automatically switches to active video source. This is for when 2 PCs are connected to HDMI for video and to USB-C for USB data only.
IF HDMI 1 video selected, USB HOST = USB-C 1 IF HDMI 2 video selected, USB HOST = USB-C 2 IF USB-C 1 video selected, USB HOST = USB-C 1 IF USB-C 2 video selected, USB HOST = USB-C 2 Note: This setting only applies when USB mode is set to LOCAL. If this property is not supported then will be returned and write to this property will be ignored.
member.exception: Value passed for USB Host is not defined in the enum .

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.DmNvxUsbInput.HostSelectionFeedback
member.summary:
Property to report the current Host USB-C port. Remote devices enumerate to the PC connected to the Host port. shall have the following behavior: USB Host automatically switches to active video source. This is for when 2 PCs are connected to HDMI for video and to USB-C for USB data only.
IF HDMI 1 video selected, USB HOST = USB-C 1 IF HDMI 2 video selected, USB HOST = USB-C 2 IF USB-C 1 video selected, USB HOST = USB-C 1 IF USB-C 2 video selected, USB HOST = USB-C 2 Note: This setting only applies when USB mode is set to LOCAL. If this property is not supported then will be returned.
The event will trigger with .

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.DmNvxUsbInput.RemoteDeviceId
member.summary: Property to specify the remote device to which the Icron device should attempt to pair.
member.remarks: Notes: 1. Takes 6 digit ID or 12 digit MAC address. A. If 6 digit, add Crestron OUI. Example: user enters 012345, the device MAC address would be 00107f012345 B. If 12 digit, its a MAC address, No additional processing needed. Example: 00-1b-13-00-83-f3 2. Should be case-insensitive 3. Should handle the following delimiters, whitespace, comma, period, dash, colon in arbitrary locations. Examples: Label on device: A71C22 Windows: 00-05-9A-3C-78-00 Linux: 52:54:00:b3:31:68 Cisco: 001d.7038.14d0 4. Note: This property is equivalent to first index of collection.

Note: This property is equivalent to first index of collection.

member.summary: Adjusts the audio source gain compensation at the L/R input up by 5 (where 5 = 0.5dB).
member.remarks: If the input remains 'true' for longer than 0.5s, the source gain compensation will auto-adjust up until the sig goes 'false' or until it reaches the max level of +10dB.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.EndpointVideoInput.AudioCompensationDown
member.summary: Adjusts the audio source gain compensation at the L/R input down by 5 (where 5 = 0.5dB).

member.summary: Sets the audio gain compensation at the L/R input

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.EndpointVideoInput.AudioCompensationUpFeedback
member.summary: Tracks the state of the corresponding up input.
member.remarks:
Valid values range from -100d (-10dB) to +100 (+10dB), adjustable in increments of 5, where 5 = 0.5dB.
A value of 0d (0dB) means that the signal will pass unaffected. Out of range will clip the compensation to the minimum or maximum values
Values not divisible by 5 will be rounded up, e.g., 12 will result in 15.

member.summary: Sets the video type of this source image. If this property is not supported then will be returned and write to this property will be ignored.
member.exception: Value passed for type control is not defined in the enum .
member.remarks: When using S-Video or composite, this input must be used to force the video type. Auto-mode will detected RGB or component video when present. Auto-mode will also allow blank video to be transmitted (for support of stand-alone audio) when no video input is present. That is, if "Source Type Control" is set to RGB, YPbPr, S-Video, or Composite, the blank frame will not be sent and audio cannot be transmitted.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.DmNvxUsbHotKey.EnterCaptureModeCustomKey
member.summary:
When is selected to .
Refer "https://wiki.osdev.org/USB_Human_Interface_Devices" for more information on the Raw USB data for each key press on the key board. Example key stroke sequence is "{LEFTCTRL}+A". Refer for the valid key strokes. Remove the prefix "Key" from the name of the key and use the remain characters in the enum constant name for each key stroke. e.g. the key stroke name for will be "A". To specify characters that aren't displayed when you press a key, such as ENTER or TAB, and keys that represent actions rather than characters, use the "Key" removed enum constant names enclosed in braces, e.g. for ENTER key it will be {ENTER}. For keys A-Z, a-z, 0-9 the characters as it is shall be entered. The USB scan codes are same for both capitals as well as small letters. This property is not supported by DMPS-4200 device.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.DmNvxUsbHotKey.EnterCaptureModeCustomKeyFeedback
member.summary:
Reports the current custom key stroke set for entry into capture mode. Raw USB data for the entry into capture mode is received to this property from the NVX device. The same is converted to the custom key stroke set and returned to the user. If the raw USB data received is not valid then {INVALID RAW USB DATA FOUND} will be returned.
The custom key is normally set when is selected to .
The event will trigger with . This property is not supported by DMPS-4200 device.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.DmNvxUsbHotKey.ExitCaptureModeCustomKeyFeedback
member.summary:
Reports the current custom key stroke set for exit from capture mode. Raw USB data for the exit from capture mode is received to this property from the NVX device. The same is converted to the custom key stroke set and returned to the user. If the raw USB data received is not valid then {INVALID RAW USB DATA FOUND} will be returned.
The custom key is normally set when is selected to .
The event will trigger with . This property is not supported by DMPS-4200 device.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.EndpointDmOutputStreamWithVideoAttributes.DisabledByHdcpFeedback
member.summary:
Indicates that the corresponding output has been disabled as the result of a failure during HDCP authentication. This occurs when HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) is detected at the input, but the display or other loopback device is not HDCP compliant. This also occurs when the maximum number of display devices that can be used with the video source (based on the application of keys and KSVs) has been exceeded.For more information about keys and KSVs, see HDCP. This is supported for some of the devices only. 'true' = Output disabled by HDCP; 'false' = Output not disabled by HDCP
The event will trigger with . This property is only supported by "HdWp4k401C".

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.EndpointDmOutputStreamWithVideoAttributes.ForceHdcpEnable
member.summary: Method to force HDCP encryption at the DM output. When enabled, the DM output will have HDCP encryption applied regardless of the HDCP state of the input signal, i.e., even if the source does not provide or require it. This method is not supported by "HdWp4k401C".

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.EndpointHdmiOutput.DisabledByHdcpFeedback
member.summary:
Indicates that the stream has been disabled as the result of a failure during HDCP authentication. This occurs when HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) is detected at the input, but the display or other loopback device is not HDCP compliant. This also occurs when the maximum number of display devices that can be used with the video source (based on the application of keys and KSVs) has been exceeded.
This property will trigger event with .
member.returns: 'true' = Output disabled by HDCP; 'false = Output not disabled by HDCP

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.EndpointScalerOutput.WallModeRaw
member.summary: Property applicable for DM-RMC-4KZ-SCALER-C Property to specifies which portion of the wall image to display in wall mode, where each display in a wall of displays shows a portion of the image. Displays can be laid out in configurations up to 8x8. Each display requires connection to a separate scaler. The wall mode can be specified using the following method: The video portion can be defined using the 4 digit decimal value WHXY where: W is the width of the wall (number of columns that make up the wall) H is the height of the wall (number of rows) X is the horizontal position of that display on the wall Y is the vertical position of that display on the wall For example, for a 2x2 video wall the upper left would be 2211d, the upper right 2221d, the lower left 2212d and the lower right 2222d. 0d disables the wall mode. *Not applicable in TXMode

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Endpoints.EndpointScalerOutput.WallModeRawFeedback
member.summary:
Property applicable for DM-RMC-4KZ-SCALER-C Reports the current wall mode position of the scaler. applicable for DM-RMC-4K-SCALER-C. The video portion can be defined using the 4 digit decimal value WHXY where: W is the width of the wall (number of columns that make up the wall) H is the height of the wall (number of rows) X is the horizontal position of that display on the wall Y is the vertical position of that display on the wall For example, for a 2x2 video wall the upper left would be 2211d, the upper right 2221d, the lower left 2212d and the lower right 2222d. 0d disables the wall mode.
The event will trigger with for this feedback.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.IHdcpOut.DisabledByHdcpFeedback
member.summary: Indicates that the corresponding output has been disabled as the result of a failure during HDCP authentication. This occurs when HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) is detected at the input, but the display or other loopback device is not HDCP compliant. This also occurs when the maximum number of display devices that can be used with the video source (based on the application of keys and KSVs) has been exceeded.For more information about keys and KSVs, see HDCP. 'true' = Output disabled by HDCP; 'false' = Output not disabled by HDCP

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eSessionInitiation.ByReceiver
member.summary: Unicast session initiated by receiver via RTSP. The DMPS3-4K-250/350C switcher's "Dmps3AirMediaInput" creates a connection to a server (transmitting device). Specify the server to which the it should connect in .

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eSessionInitiation.ByTransmitter
member.summary: Unicast session initiated by transmitter. The DMPS3-4K-250/350C switcher's "Dmps3AirMediaInput" waits for the transmitter to connect and then starts the stream. The connection source address is reported on . In this case, there is no RTSP exchange, so the decoder must be prepared to receive the stream.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eSessionInitiation.MulticastViaRTSP
member.summary: Multicast session initiated by DMPS3-4K-250/350C switcher's "Dmps3AirMediaInput" via RTSP. This is similar to mode "ByReceiver". Specify the server to which it is to connect in . In this mode DMPS3-4K-250/350C switcher's "Dmps3AirMediaInput" should NOT be configured to connect directly to the multicast address.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.eSessionInitiation.MulticastViaUDP
member.summary: Multicast raw UDP session initiation by transmitter. In this case,DMPS3-4K-250/350C switcher's "Dmps3AirMediaInput" connects to an active multicast stream. Specify the multicast address to which it should connect using .

member.summary: Pauses the stream of the input. Note: although the incoming video to the encoder is paused (frozen), the stream will continue playing and the elapsed time counter will continue in the paused state. This allows a freeze frame to be displayed if the user does not want live video to be transmitted.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Audio.Comp.AudioCompensation
member.summary: Sets the source gain compensation. Valid values range from -100 (-10dB) to +100 (+10dB). The source gain compensation only has an effect on the analog audio output (AUDIO OUT), and has no effect on the DM or HDMI outputs. The total gain at the output will never exceed 0dB, as the output range is -80dB to 0dB. If the input compensation plus the output volume exceeds 0dB, the output will be limited to 0dB. Changes that exceed 0dB will have no effect.

member.remarks: Valid values range from 0 (-80dB) to 65535 (0dB). For HD-MD-NxM-4KZE switches this property value range is: -80dB to +20 dB with 1dB increment for 10. member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Audio.Output.VolumeFeedback
member.summary:
Reports the volume level at the analog output. For HD-MD-NxM-4KZE switches this property value range is: -80dB to +20 dB with 1dB increment for 10. Default is 0dB. 200 = +20dB -800 = -80dB
The event will trigger with for the following DM devices: Dmc4kC/Dmc4kCDsp/Dmc4kHd/Dmc4kHdDsp/DmcC/DmcCat/DmcCatDsp/DmcF/DmcFDsp/DmcHd/DmcHdDsp/DmcHdo/DmcS/DmcSBase/DmcSdi/DmcSDsp.
The event will trigger with for DMOutput streams.
The event will trigger with for the CcsUcCodec200 and stand alone DMCI versions of the following DM Cards: Dmc4kC/Dmc4kCDsp/Dmc4kHd/Dmc4kHdDsp/DmcC/DmcCat/DmcCatDsp/DmcF/DmcFDsp/DmcHd/DmcHdDsp/DmcHdo/DmcS/DmcSBase/DmcSdi/DmcSDsp.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.AudioSource.ChannelsFeedback
member.summary:
Reports the number of detected audio channels accompanying the video. Values range from 0 to 8. A value of 0 signifies that no audio is present or that the channel count could not be determined.
The event will trigger with when attached to a switcher on a "DmcStr" input card.
The event will trigger with when used as a standalone DMCI "DmcStr" input card.
The event will trigger with when attached to a switcher on the "DmcStroAV" output card.
The event will trigger with when used as a standalone DMCI "DmcStroAV" output card.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.AudioSource.SamplingFreqFeedback
member.summary:

The event will trigger with .
member.remarks: Only available on the DM.Cards.DmcStroAV.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.ImageFromRemoteDrive.RefreshRate
member.summary: Property to set/get refresh rate period in minutes at which the device should check for a new image. If the period expires and the device is unable to retrieve the image, it should retry three times, waiting 30 seconds before each try. Each attempt and retry shall be reported to the field. After the three attempts, the device shall wait the period specified in refresh rate and then try again.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.ImageFromRemoteDrive.RemotePath
member.summary: Property to set/get a remote path of an image file. Only schemes HTTP and HTTPS should be supported. Ports embedded in the URI shall be supported. Queries shall be supported. Embedded usernames and passwords are not supported. If a username or username and password pair is entered into the field, the behavior is undefined and up to the HTTP client on the device. Any error should be reported to the . Path limit is 200 characters using ASCII and 100 characters using unicode.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DMInput.USBRoutedTo
member.summary:
Selects the input or output where the corresponding USB source (connected to an input slot of the switcher) will be routed. The input has no effect when USB routing is disabled ("USBEnter" = 'false'), or when USB breakaway is disabled ("EnableUSBBreakaway" = 'false'). Valid values are as follows: null = Break connection, valid DMInput or DMOutput object will assign that object.
For a DMPS3-4K-200-C and DMPS3-4K-250-C, Input USB route is not supported.
For a DMPS3-4K-300-C USB can be routed to SwitcherOutputs[3] (eDmps34K300COutputs.Dm1)and SwitcherOutputs[4] (eDmps34K300COutputs.Dm2).
For a DMPS3-4K-350-C, USB can be routed to SwitcherOutputs[3] (eDmps34K350COutputs.Dm1)and SwitcherOutputs[4] (eDmps34K350COutputs.Dm2).
member.exception: If the specified input is illegal for a USB route.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.DMInput.USBRoutedToFeedback

member.summary: Selects the input or output where the corresponding USB source (connected to an output slot of the switcher) will be routed. The input has no effect when USB routing is disabled ("USBEnter" = 'false'), or when USB breakaway is disabled ("EnableUSBBreakaway" = 'false'). member.example: Example: "switcher.Output[2].USBRoutedTo = switcher.Input[5];" Input 5 of the switcher will be routed to Output 2 of the switcher. "switcher.Output[2].USBRoutedTo = null;" Will Break; the connection on switcher Output2.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.eDmSwitch.DmMd6x1
member.summary: The DM-MD6x1 is an audio/video switcher that provides a combination of digital, analog, and DM CAT inputs and outputs.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.eDmSwitch.DmMd6x4
member.summary: The DM-MD6x4 is a DigitalMedia 8G+™ audio/video switcher and distribution center. The DM-MD6x4 provides (6) six HDMI inputs that support HDMI, DVI and DisplayPort Multimode signals types. The switcher provides (1) one HDMI output and (3) three DM 8G+ STP outputs (DigitalMedia over single shielded twisted-pair copper wire). The USB HID output port is a Type B port for connection to a USB HID-compliant host.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.eDmSwitch.DmMd6x6
member.summary: The DM-MD6x6 is a DigitalMedia 8G+™ audio/video switcher and distribution center. The DM-MD6x6 provides (6) six HDMI inputs that support HDMI, DVI and DisplayPort Multimode signal types. The switcher provides (1) one HDMI output and (5) five DM 8G+ STP outputs (DigitalMedia over single shielded twisted-pair copper wire). The USB HID output port is a Type B port for connection to a USB HID-compliant host.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.eDmSwitch.HdMd8x1
member.summary: The Crestron HD-MD8x1 is a DigitalMedia switcher that provides "audio-follows-video" switching, plus independent stereo matrix switching for audio breakaway. The switcher distributes High-Definition video and audio signals over HDMI to a video display or processor, such as the Crestron AMS. The HD-MD8X1 provides (8) HDMI 1.3a inputs (labeled INPUT 1 through INPUT 8), and (1) HDMI output (labeled OUTPUT 1).

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.eDmSwitch.HdMd8x2
member.summary: The Crestron HD-MD8x2 is a DigitalMedia switcher that provides "audio-follows-video" matrix switching, plus independent stereo matrix switching for audio breakaway. The switcher distributes High-Definition video and audio signals over HDMI to a video display or processor, such as the Crestron AMS. The HD-MD8X2 provides (8) HDMI 1.3a inputs (labeled INPUT 1 through INPUT 8), and (2) HDMI outputs (labeled OUTPUT 1 and 2).

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.eDmSwitch.DmMd8x8
member.summary:
Inputs = 8; Outputs = 8;
Crestron DigitalMedia switchers provide digital multi-channel "audio-follows-video" matrix switching, plus independent stereo matrix switching for audio breakaway. The switcher distributes uncompressed digital video and audio signals over DM, which consists of a Shielded Twisted Pair (STP), CAT5e and 4-wire DMNET. The switcher can also route any USB-capable input to any output.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.eDmSwitch.DmMd8x8rps
member.summary:
Inputs = 8; Outputs = 8;
The DM-MD-Series switcher with RPS (Redundant Power Supply) is a DigitalMedia switcher that provides digital multi-channel "audio-follows-video" matrix switching, plus independent stereo matrix switching for audio breakaway. The switcher distributes uncompressed digital video and audio signals over DM, which consists of a Shielded Twisted Pair (STP), CAT5e and 4-wire DMNET. The switcher can also route any USB data between USB hosts and devices. The DM-MD8X8-RPS provides (2) two internal 12VDC power supplies.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.eDmSwitch.DmMd64x64
member.summary:
Inputs = 64; Outputs = 64;
The DM-MD64x64 switcher is a modular matrix switcher designed for large-scale projects that integrate video, audio, networking, and control. The DM-MD64x64 switcher is equipped with a 15 inch LCD display offering complete control over system commissioning and troubleshooting, as well as the ability to preview any video or audio source. The DM-MD64x64 features a modular blade-based design which enables full matrix switching scalable from 8x8 to 64x64.

member.summary:
Inputs = 32; Outputs = 32;
Crestron DigitalMedia switchers with CPU3 Card provide digital multi-channel "audio-follows-video" matrix switching, plus independent stereo matrix switching for audio breakaway. The switcher distributes uncompressed digital video and audio signals over DM, which consists of a Shielded Twisted Pair (STP), CAT5e and 4-wire DMNET. The switcher can also route any USB-capable input to any output.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.eDmSwitch.DmMd32x32Cpu3rps
member.summary:
Inputs = 32; Outputs = 32;
The DM-MD-Series switcher with RPS (Redundant Power Supply) is a DigitalMedia switcher with CPU3 Card that provides digital multi-channel "audio-follows-video" matrix switching, plus independent stereo matrix switching for audio breakaway. The switcher distributes uncompressed digital video and audio signals over DM, which consists of a Shielded Twisted Pair (STP), CAT5e and 4-wire DMNET. The switcher can also route any USB data between USB hosts and devices. The DM-MD32X32-RPS provides (3) two internal 12VDC power supplies.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.EnableUSBBreakaway
member.summary: Enables USB breakaway for as long as the input is 'true'. This allows USB to be routed independently from video. If USB breakaway is not enabled, the USB routes will follow the selected video routes, and the "USBOut#" inputs will have no effect. 'true' (level-sensitive) = Enable USB breakaway; 'false' = Disable USB breakaway This property is not supported by HD-RX-4K-X01 switches

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.USBEnter
member.summary: Enables the "Output#_USBRoutedTo" or "Input#_USBRoutedTo" source selection analogs for as long as the input is 'true'. When the input is 'false', the analogs have no effect. 'true' (level-sensitive) = Enable USB; 'false' = Disable USB This property is not supported by HD-RX-4K-X01 switches

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.DM.Switch.VideoEnter
member.summary: Enables the "VideoOut#" video source selection analogs for as long as the input is 'true'. When the input is 'false', the analogs have no effect. 'true' (level-sensitive) = Enable video; 'false' = Disable video This property is not supported by HD-RX-4K-X01 switches

member.name: T:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.BACnet
member.summary:
BACnet class, this class is used to create the BACnet Host internally. This class implements methods to add/remove remote devices. Also implements the methods to register/unregister the BACnet slot with BACnet stack. This class defines the properties to know the current number of remote devices added, endpoint limit on the control system and current endpoint count.
This class will trigger "RemoteBACnetDevices.RemoteBACnetDevicesChange" events.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.BACnet.Register(System.UInt32,System.String,Crestron.SimplSharpPro.BACnetHostNetworkPortObject)
member.summary: Register this BACnet slot with the system. Default port number 47808 will be used for the host device. BACnet stack will be intimated about all the objects or devices that were already added to the local device/object collections so that those objects/devices will be added to the BACnet stack also.
member.param: Host Device ID.
Host Device Name.
Host Network Port Object object.
member.returns: An enum of type eDeviceRegistrationUnRegistrationResponse. An exception is thrown if an error is found while adding the host device to the BACnet stack. Will log an error if an error is found while adding a remote device, a host object or a remote object to the BACnet stack.
member.exception: Unable to add BACnet host device due to no response received or error response received from the BACnet stack.
BACnet host device with the same id is already present in the BACnet stack object/device list, so ignored the add request.
Unable to add a BACnet host device, due to the maximum number of endpoints are reached.
Host Device ID is out of range.
Host Device Name is null or empty.
"BACnetVendorList.xml" is not found under \sys folder on the control system.
member.remarks: This method will block pending a response. It is recommended to not invoke this method from within a event handler. Please launch a timer/thread to call this method. Also – this method not be called from the control system constructor.
Make sure the "BACnetVendorList.xml" is copied to the to "\sys" folder on your control system.

member.name: T:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.BACnetNetworkPortObject
member.summary: BACnet Network Port Object class. Minimum firmware version required for Network Port Object support is "2.8006.00250". Maximum number of Network Port Objects per device is 1.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.BACnetNetworkPortObject.ChangesPendingFeedback
member.summary:
This property indicates whether the configuration settings in the Network Port object map to the current configuration settings. A value of FALSE indicates that the configuration settings reflect the current port configuration information. A value of TRUE indicates the configuration settings have been modified but have not been activated on the port.
When a value is written to a property that requires activation, the value of the property shall automatically be set to TRUE, indicating that the current property values are not the values actively in use. It is necessary for the client to initiate a ReinitializeDevice service request with a 'Reinitialized State of Device' of ACTIVATE_CHANGES or WARMSTART in order to activate the currently visible configuration settings. This interaction is necessary to support atomic updating of multiple properties when modifying a network port configuration.
It is a local matter as to whether or not resetting the device by means other than a ReinitializeDevice service with a 'Reinitialized State of Device' of ACTIVATE_CHANGES or WARMSTART discards pending changes, activates pending changes, or leaves the changes pending.
It is a local matter whether, or not, a device refuses requests to write to a Network Port object if: any Network Port object has pending changes, the write request is from a device other than that which wrote the existing pending changes, and the write would result in pending changes in any Network Port object. When refusing such a request, the device shall return a Result(-) with an ‘Error Class’ of DEVICE and an ‘Error Code’ of CONFIGURATION_IN_PROGRESS.
This property will trigger event with .

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.BACnetNetworkPortObject.ReliabilityFeedback
member.summary:
This property provides an indication of whether the Network Port object, the network port, and the network connected to the port are "reliable" as far as the BACnet Device can determine and, if not, why.
Reliability of a Network Port object affects all Network Port objects that reference it directly or indirectly. If this Network Port object is otherwise not in fault, but its referenced Network Port object is, then the Reliability property shall have the value . The Reliability property default value is and is fixed. Going through the 135-2020 Clause 12.1.8 will help understand this property more.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.BACnetNetworkPortObject.NetworkNumberFeedback
member.summary: Property to report the current network number of the BACnet device. The range for this property shall be 0 to 65534. A Network Number of 0 indicates that the is not known or cannot be determined. Writing a value other than 0 shall force the property to . This property shall be writable in routers, secure devices, and any other device that requires knowledge of the network number for proper operation. If this property is writable, then a successful write to this property shall set the property to TRUE. A value written to this property shall become effective when the device receives a ReinitializeDevice service request with a 'Reinitialized State of Device' of ACTIVATE_CHANGES or WARMSTART.
