member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.BACnetRemoteNetworkPortObject.FdBBMDAddress
member.summary:
Specifies the BBMD address with which the local device registers as a foreign device when is set to .
The string format shall be as follows: if the BBMD IP address is 10.88.12.16 and its port number is 47808, then the value shall be "0A:58:0C:10:BA:C0".
This string can also be a combination of hostname and port number. The value shall be "CP4N-00107F9CC2BA:BA:C0", where "CP4N-00107F9CC2BA" represents the hostname of the BBMD and "BA:C0" represents the port number of the BBMD, whose value shall be 0xBAC0 (47808 in decimal).
IP address 0.0.0.0, 255.255.255.255 (broadcast address), multicast addresses (224.0.0.0–239.255.255.255), and loopback address (127.0.0.0/8) are not valid.
The IP address octets shall be converted to hexadecimal format, with each octet separated by a colon (":"). Then, the BBMD port number shall be converted to hexadecimal, split into two bytes separated by a colon, and appended to the IP address string. Valid port numbers are from 1024 to 65535.
In the case of a hostname plus port number combination, the hostname string and the port number are separated by a colon (":"). The BBMD port number shall then be converted to hexadecimal, split into two bytes separated by a colon, and appended to the hostname string. The maximum length limitation for the hostname and port number combination is 231 characters.
member.example:
For IP address 10.88.12.16 and port 47808: IP in hex: 0A:58:0C:10 Port in hex: BA:C0 Combined string: "0A:58:0C:10:BA:C0"
For hostname CP4N-00107F9CC2BA and port 47808: Port in hex: BA:C0 Combined string: "CP4N-00107F9CC2BA:BA:C0"

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.BACnetRemoteNetworkPortObject.FdBBMDAddressFeedback
member.summary:
This property indicates the BBMD with which the local device is to register as a foreign device when is . This property shall be present and writable if is on the remote device’s Network Port Object.
If this property is writable, then a successful write to it shall set the property to TRUE.
This property will trigger the event with .
This property value is populated when the value is received from the remote device’s Network Port Object.
As with the property, this property shall also consist of an IP address plus port number combination, or a hostname plus port number combination.

member.name: P:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.BACnetRemoteNetworkPortObject.FdSubscriptionLifetime
member.summary: This property is to set the Time-To-Live value, in seconds, to be used in the Register-Foreign-Device BVLL message. This property shall be present and writable if is . If this property is writable, then a successful write to this property shall set the property to TRUE. A value written to this property shall become effective when the device receives a ReinitializeDevice service request with a 'Reinitialized State of Device' of ACTIVATE_CHANGES or WARMSTART.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronDeviceWithEvents.ParseIrInDataFromStructure(System.Byte*,System.UInt32)
member.summary: Version of ParseDataFromStructure used by IR devices. For an IR Slot, there should only be one level of encapsulation. If a packet ID CNT 09 00 00 00 is received, this is a all clear. Clear all of the High joins on all devices currently on the IR Input. If the packet is not an all clear attempt to find the device from the ID returned by the Parsing function. If the returned ID is a phantom ID, not in the system, look for the next device at a lower ID and send the data there.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpPro.CrestronDeviceWithEvents.GrabDeviceFromIncomingIrInEncapsulatedPacket(Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.CSSPDeviceProtocol.CParsedPacketData)
member.summary: Version of GrabDeviceFromIncomingEncapsulatedPacket used by IR devices. Overridden Function to grab the device from an incoming encapsulated packet For a IRInputSlot, there is only going to be one level of hierarchy. The ID at that level is the ID of the device received, if the ID is phantom the correct ID is determined by the caller of this function.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.CSSPDeviceProtocol.MaxDigitalsInAPacket
member.summary: (Assumption of 127 bytes max in a packet due to some brain-dead devices that treat the count byte as a signed byte) 3 bytes overhead + 20 levels of encapsulation @ 3 bytes each = 63 bytes overhead. 127-63 = 64 bytes. 64/2 bytes per digital join/state = 32 per packet.

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.CSSPDeviceProtocol.MaxAnalogsInAPacket
member.summary: (Assumption of 127 bytes max in a packet due to some brain-dead devices that treat the count byte as a signed byte) 3 bytes overhead + 20 levels of encapsulation @ 3 bytes each = 63 bytes overhead. 127-63 = 64 bytes. 64/4 bytes per digital join/state = 16 per packet (round down).

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.CSSPDeviceProtocol.Max16bParametersInAPacket
member.summary: (Assumption of 127 bytes max in a packet due to some brain-dead devices that treat the count byte as a signed byte) 3 bytes overhead + 20 levels of encapsulation @ 3 bytes each = 63 bytes overhead. 127-63 = 64 bytes. 64/4 = bytes per digital join/state = 10 per packet (round down).

member.name: F:Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.CSSPDeviceProtocol.Max32bParametersInAPacket
member.summary: (Assumption of 127 bytes max in a packet due to some brain-dead devices that treat the count byte as a signed byte) 3 bytes overhead + 20 levels of encapsulation @ 3 bytes each = 63 bytes overhead. 127-63 = 64 bytes. 64/6 = bytes per digital join/state = 10 per packet (round down).

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.CSSPDeviceProtocol.IdWidthAtPreviousEncapsulationLevel_Build(System.Collections.Generic.List{Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.HierarchyDataStruct})
member.summary: This will determine the ID width of the primary packet based upon the last layer of encapsulation. For example, if the we have a digital, id 03 00 05 80, and last layer of encapsulation is a type 0x38 (which is a complex join, then the id of the packet will have to be 4 bytes wide. If it's a standard encpsulation like a type 0x20 then it's just a byte wide. If there's on encapsulation, it's 1 byte wide.
member.remarks: In the future, EVERY function that calls IdWidthAtPreviousEncapsulationLevel_Build() should be updated to call ComputeIdWidth() instead, passing Device.ID as the second argument.
member.param: The hierarchy to to work with

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.CSSPDeviceProtocol.ComputeIdWidth(System.Collections.Generic.List{Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.HierarchyDataStruct},System.UInt32)
member.summary: This will determine the ID width of the primary packet based upon the last layer of encapsulation. For example, if the we have a digital, id 03 00 05 80, and last layer of encapsulation is a type 0x38 (which is a complex join, then the id of the packet will have to be 4 bytes wide. If it's a standard encapsulation like a type 0x20 or none, then it will look at the DeviceId and if that is greater than 255, it will be a 4 byte wide ID other wise 1 byte. (This is used currently for Bacnet support.)
member.remarks: In the future, EVERY function that calls IdWidthAtPreviousEncapsulationLevel_Build() should be updated to call ComputeIdWidth() instead, passing Device.ID as the second argument.

member.summary: Register the device with the system. Port needs to be registered with the system when it is part of the control system or a three series card. member.remarks: Registering a port device does not register the parent. Please use the register function on the parent device.

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.PortDevice.UnRegister
member.summary: Function to unregister a port with the system. For control system ports this needs to be done to release the port for other programs to use. For ports apart of a 3-Series cards, the card needs to first be unregistered and then this function can be used. For ports apart of CEN-IO devices, this can be called at any time as dynamic registration is supported.
member.returns: Returns eDeviceRegistrationUnRegistrationResponse indicating success or failure.

member.summary: Function to check and see if a join is gated for transmit during normal operation (not update request).

member.name: M:Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.DeviceBasis.IsJoinGatedToTransmit(System.UInt32,Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.eSignalTypeEnum,Crestron.SimplSharpProInternal.CSSPDeviceProtocol.ePacketType,System.Int32)
member.summary:
Function to check and see if a join is gated for transmit during normal operations or update request. 1. Is this device a Smart object AND we're looking at an analog/digital/serial join? -OR- 2. Is this a conventional device without a page join update class? -OR- 3. We have a device with page join gating information in the hierarchy AND this join is gated to transmit based on the gating information.
If any of 1, 2, 3 are true, then it's gated to transmit.
member.param: The join number
A signal type from the eSignalTypeEnum class
Update reuqest type from the CSSPDeviceProtocol.ePacketType class. If not during update request time, use case CSSPDeviceProtocol.ePacketType.e_PktUpdateRequestProcessNormally
The type of send from the TLDM_INTERFACE_Constants class. If not during update request time, use TLDM_INTERFACE_Constants.TLDM_SEND_MSG_TYPE_NORMAL_SEND.
